claims.source: Whereas NDUFA2 knockout in HEK293T cells results in the loss of the N-module and complete loss of CI activity (Stroud et al., 2016), NDUFA2 knock-down in D. melanogaster has minimal effects, with CI retaining ~97% of WT (Mhc-Gal4/W1118 flies) activity during the first week after eclosing as adults (Garcia et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous functional study in D. melanogaster.

claims.claim: NDUFA2 only interacts with NDUFS1.
claims.source: Given that NDUFA2 only interacts with NDUFS1, it was proposed that NDUFA2 binding compensates for truncation of NDUFS1's 'D domain' that is otherwise present in bacterial orthologs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, C; Padavannil et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural data and citation to a previous proposal.

claims.claim: Domain D remains short in Dm-NDUFS1 like other eukaryotes.
claims.source: However, like other eukaryotes, domain D remains short in Dm-NDUFS1 and the reason for the sustained stability of Dm-CI when NDUFA2 is knocked down is unclear.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural data and represents an observation about an unresolved question.

claims.claim: NDUFS7 in D. melanogaster has an extended N-terminus relative to mammalian CI, as in Y. lipolytica.
claims.source: As in Y. lipolytica, NDUFS7 in D. melanogaster has an extended N-terminus relative to mammalian CI (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison data.

claims.claim: The N-terminus of Dm-NDUFS7 is flipped ~180° relative to Yl-NDUFS7, binding overtop of NDUFA12 instead of along the surface of NDUFA9.
claims.source: However, whereas the N-terminus of Yl-NDUFS7 binds along the surface of NDUFA9, that of Dm-CI is flipped ~180° binding overtop of NDUFA12 (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison data.

claims.claim: The additional interface between NDUFS7 and NDUFA12 would stabilize the association of NDUFA12 in Dm-CI.
claims.source: This additional interface would stabilize the association of NDUFA12 in Dm-CI.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observation of additional interactions.

claims.claim: During CI assembly, the assembly factor NDUFAF2 binds at the equivalent position of NDUFA12 and is exchanged for NDUFA12 before the full assembly of the PA.
claims.source: During CI assembly, the assembly factor NDUFAF2 binds at the equivalent position of NDUFA12 (Parey et al., 2019) and is exchanged for NDUFA12 before the full assembly of the PA (Andrews et al., 2013; Vogel et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous assembly studies.

claims.claim: The additional interactions between NDUFS7 and NDUFA12 in Dm-CI may influence the assembly of the PA by promoting the exchange of NDUFAF2 with NDUFA12 through the stabilization of NDUFA12 binding.
claims.source: The additional interactions between NDUFS7 and NDUFA12 in Dm-CI may thus influence the assembly of the PA by promoting the exchange of NDUFAF2 with NDUFA12 through the stabilization of NDUFA12 binding (Figure 2B).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on structural data and knowledge of assembly pathways.

claims.claim: Dm-ND2 lacks three TMHs at the N-terminus, thus having 11 TMHs as opposed to the 14 TMHs otherwise seen in bacteria, plants, ciliates, and yeast.
claims.source: As in mammalian CI, Dm-ND2 lacks three TMHs at the N-terminus, thus having 11 TMHs as opposed to the 14 TMHs otherwise seen in bacteria, plants, ciliates, and yeast (Birrell and Hirst, 2010; Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 3A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural data and citation to a previous comparative study.

claims.claim: The cavity formed by the lack of the three TMHs in ND2 is filled with lipids that are held in place in part by the NDUFC2 subunit.
claims.source: The cavity formed by the lack of the three TMHs is filled with lipids that are held in place in part by the NDUFC2 subunit (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural data showing lipid binding.

claims.claim: The last TMH in Dm-ND2 (TMH11ND2) has two additional turns compared to TMH11ND2 of mammals.
claims.source: Similar to other eukaryotic CIs, the last TMH in Dm-ND2 (TMH11ND2), has two additional turns, compared to TMH11ND2 of mammals (Figure 2D and Figure 2—figure supplement 3B; Klusch et al., 2021; Parey et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison data and citations.

claims.claim: It has been proposed that in mammals, subunit NDUFC1 plays a role in shortening TMH11ND2 by binding a cardiolipin molecule that caps the helix stabilizing its partially unwound state.
claims.source: It has been proposed that in mammals, subunit NDUFC1 plays a role in shortening TMH11ND2 by binding a cardiolipin molecule that caps the helix stabilizing its partially unwound state (Padavannil et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous proposal.

claims.claim: D. melanogaster lacks accessory subunit NDUFC1 and has a longer TMH11ND2 relative to mammals, supporting the proposed role of NDUFC1 in mammals.
claims.source: Given that D. melanogaster lacks accessory subunit NDUFC1 and has a longer TMH11ND2 relative to mammals, this supports the proposed role of NDUFC1 in mammals.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on structural comparison supporting a previous hypothesis.

claims.claim: Lack of NDUFC1 in Dm-CI indicates that it was recruited as an accessory subunit only after the split of Protostomia and Deuterostomia.
claims.source: Lack of NDUFC1 in Dm-CI also indicates that it was recruited as an accessory subunit only after the split of Protostomia and Deuterostomia.
claims.evidence: This is an inference about evolution based on the absence of NDUFC1 in Dm-CI.

claims.claim: In both mammals and D. melanogaster, the TMH10-11ND2 loop provides a major interface with the metazoan-specific subunit NDUFA10.
claims.source: In both mammals and D. melanogaster, the TMH10-11ND2 loop provides a major interface with the metazoan-specific subunit NDUFA10 (Figure 2E and Video 4).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural data.

claims.claim: In Y. lipolytica, which lacks any subunit binding on the matrix side of ND2, the TMH10-11ND2 loop spans across the matrix surface of ND2 as a coil.
claims.source: In Y. lipolytica, which lacks any subunit binding on the matrix side of ND2, as well as in plants and Tetrahymena which use the equivalent loop to interact with their γ-carbonic anhydrase subunit (Klusch et al., 2021; Maldonado et al., 2020; Soufari et al., 2020; Zhou et al., 2022), the TMH10-11ND2 loop spans across the matrix surface of ND2 as a coil.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claims.claim: In mammals, TMH10-11ND2 spans the same distance across the matrix surface but forms a short α-helix that interacts directly with NDUFA10.
claims.source: In mammals, TMH10-11ND2 spans the same distance across the matrix surface but forms a short α-helix that interacts directly with NDUFA10 (Figure 2D and E and Video 4).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural data.

claims.claim: The length of the TMH10-11ND2 loop is only shorter by two residues in D. melanogaster compared to mammals.
claims.source: Given that the length of the TMH10-11ND2 loop is only shorter by two residues in D. melanogaster compared to mammals (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B), the additional residues required for the TMH10-11ND2 loop to fold into an α-helix in mammals must come from the unwinding of TMH11ND2.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment data.

claims.claim: The additional residues required for the TMH10-11ND2 loop to fold into an α-helix in mammals must come from the unwinding of TMH11ND2.
claims.source: Given that the length of the TMH10-11ND2 loop is only shorter by two residues in D. melanogaster compared to mammals (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B), the additional residues required for the TMH10-11ND2 loop to fold into an α-helix in mammals must come from the unwinding of TMH11ND2.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on structural and sequence comparison.

claims.claim: The mammalian interface between ND2 and NDUFA10 cannot form before NDUFC1 binds and recruits a cardiolipin to partially unwind TMH11ND2.
claims.source: Thus, a simple model emerges for how mammalian CI is dependent on NDUFC1 for assembly. Namely, the mammalian interface between ND2 and NDUFA10 cannot form before NDUFC1 binds and recruits a cardiolipin to partially unwind TMH11ND2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C; Padavannil et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is a model proposed based on structural inference and citation to previous work.

claims.claim: This model is consistent with the known binding order and dependencies of NDUFC1 and NDUFA10 to ND2 during CI assembly.
claims.source: This model is consistent with the known binding order and dependencies of NDUFC1 and NDUFA10 to ND2 during CI assembly (Guerrero-Castillo et al., 2017; Stroud et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous assembly studies.

claims.claim: In Dm-CI, due to an extended C-terminal coil, the MA accessory subunit NDUFA11 has much more extensive interaction with the core subunits than seen in mammals.
claims.source: In Dm-CI, due to an extended C-terminal coil, the MA accessory subunit NDUFA11 has much more extensive interaction with the core subunits than seen in mammals (Figure 2F, Figure 2—figure supplement 4A and B and Video 5).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison data.

claims.claim: In mammalian CI, only limited protein-protein contacts between NDUFA11 and other CI subunits are observed, dominated mainly by its short C-terminal coil.
claims.source: In mammalian CI, only limited protein-protein contacts between NDUFA11 and other CI subunits are observed, dominated mainly by its short C-terminal coil (Figure 2F and Figure 2—figure supplement 4A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural data from mammalian CI.

claims.claim: Detergent extraction can result in the loss of NDUFA11 in mammals, resulting in so-called 'state 3' particles.
claims.source: For this reason, detergent extraction can result in the loss of NDUFA11 in mammals, resulting in so-called 'state 3' particles (Chung et al., 2022b; Fiedorczuk et al., 2016; Zhu et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claims.claim: In the fungus Y. lipolytica the C-terminus of NDUFA11 is much longer and extends along the matrix side of the complex.
claims.source: However, in the fungus Y. lipolytica the C-terminus of NDUFA11 is much longer and extends along the matrix side of the complex (Parey et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous structural study.

claims.claim: NDUFA11 in Y. lipolytica is harder to dissociate from the complex even after treatment with harsh detergents.
claims.source: Likely for this reason NDUFA11 in Y. lipolytica is harder to dissociate from the complex even after treatment with harsh detergents (Angerer et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous biochemical study and represents an inference about the structural basis.

claims.claim: The C-terminus of Dm-NDUFA11 runs across the membrane arm, tucking between NDUFB5, NDUFS5, NDUFA8, and ND2, emerging adjacent to NDUFC2 on the opposite side.
claims.source: However, unlike the C-terminus in Y. lipolytica NDUFA11 which runs along the length of the MA, that of Dm-NDUFA11 runs across the membrane arm (i.e. perpendicular to the long axis), tucking between NDUFB5, NDUFS5, NDUFA8, and ND2, emerging adjacent to NDUFC2 on the opposite side (Figure 2F and Video 5).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural data.

claims.claim: This arrangement of Dm-NDUFA11 is not seen in any other known CI structure.
claims.source: This arrangement is not seen in any other known CI structure.
claims.evidence: This is a comparative statement based on knowledge of other CI structures.

claims.claim: The C-terminus of Dm-NDUFA11 occupies space that is occupied by subunit NDUX1 (NUXM) in yeast, plants, and ciliates.
claims.source: The C-terminus of Dm-NDUFA11 occupies space that is occupied by subunit NDUX1 (NUXM) in yeast, plants, and ciliates (a subunit that is lost in metazoans along with the truncation of ND2), and the N-terminus of NDUFC2 in mammals (Fiedorczuk et al., 2016; Klusch et al., 2021; Maldonado et al., 2020; Parey et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2022).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural comparison and citations.

claims.claim: Mammalian CI is assembled through a series of intermediates and NDUFA11 is a terminally associated protein that does not form a part of any assembly intermediate.
claims.source: Mammalian CI is assembled through a series of intermediates and NDUFA11 is a terminally associated protein that does not form a part of any assembly intermediate (Guerrero-Castillo et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous assembly study.

claims.claim: In mammals, NDUFB5, NDUFB8, and NDUFS5 on the IMS side are all present in assembly intermediates prior to the addition of NDUFA11.
claims.source: Also in mammals, NDUFB5, NDUFB8, and NDUFS5 on the IMS side are all present in assembly intermediates prior to the addition of NDUFA11 (Guerrero-Castillo et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous assembly study.

claims.claim: The arrangement seen in Dm-CI suggests that Dm-NDUFA11 would need to bind Dm-ND2 before Dm-NDUFB5, Dm-NDUFA8, and Dm-NDUFS5.
claims.source: The arrangement seen in Dm-CI, in which the C-terminus of Dm-NDUFA11 is sandwiched between Dm-NDUFB5, Dm-NDUFA8, Dm-NDUFS5, and Dm-ND2 (Video 5), suggests that Dm-NDUFA11 would need to bind Dm-ND2 before Dm-NDUFB5, Dm-NDUFA8, and Dm-NDUFS5.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on structural data about assembly order.

claims.claim: ND5 would need to associate with ND2 before NDUA11 could bind because NDUFA11 binds on top of ND5-HL.
claims.source: However, as NDUFA11 binds on top of ND5-HL, ND5 would need to associate with ND2 before NDUA11 could bind.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on structural data about assembly order.

claims.claim: This order of events is counter to what occurs in mammals and indicates that assembly of this region of Dm-CI might proceed via a distinct mechanism than that of mammals.
claims.source: This order of events is counter to what occurs in mammals (Guerrero-Castillo et al., 2017) and indicates that like plant CI (Ligas et al., 2018), assembly of this region of Dm-CI might proceed via a distinct mechanism than that of mammals.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on structural comparison and citations to assembly studies.

claims.claim: In mammals there are two isoforms of the NDFUV3 subunit – a long isoform NDUFV3-L and a short isoform NDUFV3-S.
claims.source: In mammals there are two isoforms of the NDFUV3 subunit – a long isoform NDUFV3-L and a short isoform NDUFV3-S – and it has been proposed that binding of the different isoforms may impact the activity of CI (Bridges et al., 2016; Dibley et al., 2017; Guerrero-Castillo et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: It has been proposed that binding of the different NDUFV3 isoforms may impact the activity of CI.
claims.source: In mammals there are two isoforms of the NDFUV3 subunit – a long isoform NDUFV3-L and a short isoform NDUFV3-S – and it has been proposed that binding of the different isoforms may impact the activity of CI (Bridges et al., 2016; Dibley et al., 2017; Guerrero-Castillo et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies proposing this regulatory mechanism.

claims.claim: Density for a subunit at the position of NDUFV3 in mammals was observed in the Dm-CI structure.
claims.source: Density for a subunit at the position of NDUFV3 in mammals was also observed in the Dm-CI structure (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural data.

claims.claim: In the average structure calculated using all Dm-CI particles, the NDUFV3 density was weak compared to that of the surrounding core subunits.
claims.source: However, in the average structure calculated using all Dm-CI particles, this density was weak compared to that of the surrounding core subunits.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural data analysis.

claims.claim: When focused refinements were performed with a mask around the tip of the PA, two clear classes could be isolated differing in the occupancy of the NDUFV3 site.
claims.source: When focused refinements were performed with a mask around the tip of the PA, two clear classes could be isolated differing in the occupancy of the NDUFV3 site (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by cryoEM data processing and classification.

claims.claim: In Dm-CI the NDUFV3 site is only partially occupied.
claims.source: Thus, in Dm-CI this site is only partially occupied.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the classification showing different occupancy states.

claims.claim: The 68 kDa fragment of the atypical cadherin (Ft4) can regulate Dm-CI activity.
claims.source: The 68 kDa fragment of the atypical cadherin (Ft4) can regulate Dm-CI activity (Sing et al., 2014) and it was proposed that it may bind to Dm-CI at the NDUFV3 site (Bridges et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous functional studies.

claims.claim: It was proposed that Ft4 may bind to Dm-CI at the NDUFV3 site.
claims.source: The 68 kDa fragment of the atypical cadherin (Ft4) can regulate Dm-CI activity (Sing et al., 2014) and it was proposed that it may bind to Dm-CI at the NDUFV3 site (Bridges et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous proposal.

claims.claim: The results are consistent with the hypothesis that binding at the NDUFV3 site may be regulatory.
claims.source: The density of the occupied class was too noisy to confidently assign the sequence of the subunit from the map (Figure 3A). However, our results are consistent with the hypothesis that binding at this site may be regulatory (Bridges et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on structural data supporting a previous hypothesis.

claims.claim: In mammals NDUFA10 forms a state-dependent interface with accessory subunit NDUFA5.
claims.source: In addition to the major interface between NDUFA10 and ND2, in mammals NDUFA10 forms a state-dependent interface with accessory subunit NDUFA5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A; Agip et al., 2018; Kampjut and Sazanov, 2020; Letts et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claims.claim: In Dm-CI, the interface between NDUFA10 and NDUFA5 is larger due to an extended NDUFA10 N-terminal coil that inserts between NDUFA10 and NDUFA5.
claims.source: In Dm-CI, the interface between NDUFA10 and NDUFA5 is larger due to an extended NDUFA10 N-terminal coil that inserts between NDUFA10 and NDUFA5 (Figure 3B and C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by structural data.

claims.claim: The enhanced interface between Dm-NDUFA10 and Dm-NDUFA5 would make these subunits more difficult to separate.
claims.source: The enhanced interface between Dm-NDUFA10 and Dm-NDUFA5 would make these subunits more difficult to separate and indicates that, although the interactions at this interface may be state-dependent (see below), the interface is less likely to be fully broken as seen in the mammalian context (Agip et al., 2018; Kampjut and Sazanov, 2020; Letts et al., 2019).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on structural data.

claims.claim: In mammals, the N-terminus of NDUFB4 forms part of the only matrix interface between CI and CIII2 in SC I+III2.
claims.source: In mammals, the N-terminus of NDUFB4 forms part of the only matrix interface between CI and CIII2 in SC I+III2 (Letts et al., 2019; Letts and Sazanov, 2017).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies of supercomplexes.

claims.claim: In this interaction, a loop from the UQRC1 subunit of one CIII protomer binds in between the N-terminus of NDUFB4 and the three-helix-bundle of subunit NDUFB9.
claims.source: In this interaction, a loop from the UQRC1 subunit of one CIII protomer binds in between the N-terminus of NDUFB4 and the three-helix-bundle of subunit NDUFB9.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by knowledge of supercomplex structures.

claims.claim: In Dm-CI the N-terminus of Dm-NDUFB4 is truncated relative to that of mammals and does not extend far enough towards NDUFB9 to form this interface.

claims.claim: The lack of the NDUFB4-CIII2 interface likely contributes to the observed low abundance of SCs in D. melanogaster mitochondria.

claims.claim: It has been proposed that NDUFA11's interaction with CI may have been weakened in species, such as mammals, to promote SC formation by requiring the presence of CIII2 to hold NDUFA11 in place.
claims.source: Additionally, given its role in bridging between CI and CIII2 in respiratory SCs (Letts et al., 2019; Letts and Sazanov, 2017), it has been proposed that NDUFA11's interaction with CI may have been weakened in species, such as mammals, to promote SC formation by requiring the presence of CIII2 to hold NDUFA11 in place (Padavannil et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies and a proposal.

claims.claim: The extended interaction interface provided by the C-terminus of Dm-NDUFA11 indicates that Dm-NDUFA11 is not dependent on the presence of CIII2 for its stable association with the Dm-CI.
claims.source: The extended interaction interface provided by the C-terminus of Dm-NDUFA11 indicates that Dm-NDUFA11 is not dependent on the presence of CIII2 for its stable association with the Dm-CI.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on structural data.

claims.claim: The Dm-CI structure supports the proposed inverse relationship between the strength of the interaction between NDUFA11 and CI and the abundance of SCs.
claims.source: Thus, the Dm-CI structure supports the proposed inverse relationship between the strength of the interaction between NDUFA11 and CI and the abundance of SCs (Padavannil et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on structural data supporting a previous proposal.

claims.claim: Lipids form an integral part of the CI MA and loss of lipids during purification results in diminished CI activity.
claims.source: Lipids form an integral part of the CI MA and loss of lipids during purification results in diminished CI activity (Letts et al., 2016a; Padavannil et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claims.claim: Across species, structural lipids are seen tightly binding to the surface of CI at the interface of the core H+-pumping subunits.
claims.source: Across species, structural lipids are seen tightly binding to the surface of CI at the interface of the core H+-pumping subunits and specific deformation of the lipid membrane by NDUFA9 occurs adjacent to the Q-tunnel (Kampjut and Sazanov, 2020; Parey et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2022).

claims.claim: Specific deformation of the lipid membrane by NDUFA9 occurs adjacent to the Q-tunnel.

claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claims.claim: The pattern of lipid binding to Dm-CI is like that seen in other CI structures with two notable exceptions.

claims.claim: Dm-ND5 lacks the first TMH for a total of only 15 TMHs instead of 16 TMHs observed in ND5 of Y. lipolytica and mammals.

claims.claim: Loss of the first TMH of ND5 must have occurred after the split of Protostomia and Deuterostomia because mammalian ND5 maintains its full complement of helices.

claims.claim: In Dm-CI the space under ND2 is filled by the C-terminus of NDUFA11.

claims.claim: The N-terminus of Dm-NDUFC2 crosses over the C-terminal coil of NDUFA8 and forms additional interactions with NDUFB1 and NDUFB5.

claims.claim: The classes differ in the presence of an ordered α-helical element from NDUFS4 bound at the interface of NDUFA5, NDUFA10, and NDUFA6 and in the angle between the PA and MA.

results.result: D. melanogaster complex I (Dm-CI) does not exhibit a NEM-sensitive deactive state but shows slow activation kinetics indicative of an off-pathway resting state that is insensitive to both NEM and MgCl2.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C29, C30, C36, C37, C38, C41, and C42 collectively demonstrate through experimental data (Figure 1B, C, E, G, and supplementary figures) that Dm-CI lacks NEM sensitivity after deactivation but exhibits activation lag phases insensitive to NEM and MgCl2. Claims C31 and C32 provide mechanistic interpretation supported by structural data and citations. The biochemical characterization is rigorous with appropriate controls (porcine CI) and multiple experimental conditions.

results.result: The structure of Dm-CI was resolved to 3.3 Å resolution, revealing 43 subunits (14 core and 29 accessory), with NDUFA2 and NDUFC1 absent, and conserved electron transfer pathway and proton-pumping machinery.
results.evaluation: Claims C43-C52 are supported by cryoEM data (Figure 1H, Table 1, supplementary figures) showing structural determination at 3.3 Å with detailed subunit composition analysis. The identification of missing subunits (C46, C51, C52) and conservation of catalytic machinery (C48, C50) is well-documented through structural comparison and citations to previous studies. The resolution and model statistics in Table 1 support the structural claims.

results.result: A previously uncharacterized protein (Dme1_CG9034, isoform B) was identified as the NDUFA3 ortholog in D. melanogaster based on structural density and amino acid assignment.
results.evaluation: Claims C55-C57 are supported by structural data (Figure 1—figure supplement 6) showing density at the NDUFA3 position and sequence analysis identifying CG9034. The identification is corroborated by previous proteomic data (C57, Garcia et al., 2017) showing CG9034 co-migrates with Dm-CI. The structural and proteomic evidence converge to support this novel identification.

results.result: The NDUFS1 loop (residues 665-685) lacks the α-helix found in other species, which may explain the absence of NDUFA2 in Dm-CI structure, though the functional significance remains unclear given minimal effects of NDUFA2 knockdown in D. melanogaster.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C61 are supported by structural comparison data (Figure 2A, supplementary figures) and sequence alignments showing the loop is shorter and lacks secondary structure. Claims C62-C63 provide functional context through citations to previous studies. However, C65 acknowledges uncertainty about the sustained stability of Dm-CI without NDUFA2, indicating this is an area requiring further investigation. The structural observations are solid, but mechanistic understanding is incomplete.

results.result: The N-terminus of Dm-NDUFS7 is flipped ~180° relative to Y. lipolytica, binding overtop of NDUFA12 instead of along NDUFA9, which may stabilize NDUFA12 association and influence peripheral arm assembly.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C67 are supported by structural comparison data (Figure 2B, supplementary figures). Claim C68 is a reasonable inference about stabilization based on additional interface formation. Claims C69-C70 integrate knowledge of assembly pathways (citations provided) with structural observations to propose a mechanism for assembly regulation. The structural data is clear, and the assembly implications are logically derived.

results.result: Dm-ND2 lacks three N-terminal TMHs (having 11 instead of 14), with the cavity filled by lipids and NDUFC2. The absence of NDUFC1 in Dm-CI and longer TMH11ND2 supports the proposed role of NDUFC1 in mammals for shortening TMH11ND2 and enabling NDUFA10 binding.
results.evaluation: Claims C71-C73 are supported by structural data (Figure 2C, D, supplementary figures) and citations. Claims C74-C76 integrate structural observations with previous proposals (Padavannil et al., 2021) to support evolutionary inferences. Claims C77-C83 provide detailed structural and sequence analysis (Figure 2E, supplementary figures) supporting a model for mammalian CI assembly dependence on NDUFC1. The model is consistent with known assembly dependencies (C83), making this a well-supported result.

results.result: Dm-NDUFA11 has an extended C-terminus that runs across the membrane arm, creating more extensive interactions with core subunits than in mammals, suggesting a distinct assembly mechanism for this region in Dm-CI.
results.evaluation: Claims C84-C91 are supported by structural comparison data (Figure 2F, Video 5, supplementary figures) showing the unique arrangement of Dm-NDUFA11. Claims C92-C96 integrate knowledge of mammalian assembly pathways (citations provided) with structural observations to infer differences in Dm-CI assembly. The structural data clearly shows the distinct arrangement, and the assembly implications are logically derived from the structural constraints, though direct experimental validation of the proposed assembly order is not provided.

results.result: The NDUFV3 site in Dm-CI is only partially occupied, as revealed by focused refinement showing two classes differing in NDUFV3 occupancy, consistent with a potential regulatory role for binding at this site.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C102 are supported by structural data and cryoEM classification (Figure 3A, supplementary figure). Claims C103-C105 provide context from previous studies about Ft4 regulation and support the hypothesis of regulatory binding at this site. The structural evidence for partial occupancy is clear from the classification results, and the regulatory interpretation is consistent with previous proposals, though direct functional validation is not provided.

results.result: The interface between NDUFA10 and NDUFA5 in Dm-CI is larger than in mammals due to an extended NDUFA10 N-terminal coil, making these subunits more difficult to separate and indicating the interface is less likely to be fully broken.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C107 are supported by structural comparison data (Figure 3B, C, supplementary figures) and citations to previous mammalian studies. Claim C108 is a reasonable inference about the functional consequence of the enhanced interface. The structural observations are clear, and the inference about reduced separation is logical based on increased interaction surface area.

results.result: The N-terminus of Dm-NDUFB4 is truncated relative to mammals and does not extend far enough to form the matrix interface with CIII2, likely contributing to the low abundance of supercomplexes in D. melanogaster mitochondria.
results.evaluation: Claims C109-C111 are supported by structural comparison data (Figure 3D, supplementary figures) and citations to previous supercomplex structures. Claim C112 is an inference connecting the structural observation to the biochemical observation of low SC abundance. The structural data clearly shows the truncation, and the inference about SC abundance is reasonable, though direct experimental validation of this causal relationship is not provided.

results.result: The extended C-terminus of Dm-NDUFA11 provides a more extensive interaction interface, indicating Dm-NDUFA11 is not dependent on CIII2 for stable association with CI, supporting an inverse relationship between NDUFA11-CI interaction strength and SC abundance.
results.evaluation: Claims C113-C115 integrate structural observations about Dm-NDUFA11 (from previous result) with previous proposals (Padavannil et al., 2021) about the relationship between NDUFA11 binding and SC formation. The inference (C114) is logical based on the structural data, and C115 connects this to the broader hypothesis. The structural evidence supports the inference, though direct experimental validation of the proposed relationship is not provided.

results.result: Dm-ND5 lacks the first TMH (having 15 instead of 16), with the region occupied by lipid instead of protein, and this deletion must have occurred after the Protostomia/Deuterostomia split.
results.evaluation: Claims C120-C121 are supported by structural data (Figure 3E, supplementary figures) showing the absence of TMH1 and lipid binding in that region. Claim C122 is an evolutionary inference based on the presence of all 16 TMHs in mammalian ND5. The structural observations are clear, and the evolutionary inference is logical, though the functional implications and distribution across Protostomia remain to be determined as noted in the text.

results.result: Dm-NDUFC2 has an extended N-terminus that crosses over the C-terminal coil of NDUFA8 and forms additional interactions with NDUFB1 and NDUFB5, contributing to lipid binding at the ND2/ND4 interface.
results.evaluation: Claims C125-C126 are supported by structural comparison data (Figure 2C, supplementary figures) showing the extended N-terminus and its interactions. Claim C127 is an inference about the functional role of these interactions in stabilizing lipid binding. The structural observations are clear, and the inference about lipid stabilization is reasonable based on the structural arrangement.

results.result: Focused classification revealed a helix-locked state with an ordered NDUFS4 α-helix wedged between the peripheral and membrane arms, and flexible states lacking this helix, with 3DVA showing a smooth transition between states.
results.evaluation: Claims C128-C131 are supported by cryoEM classification data (Figure 4, supplementary figures) showing distinct classes. Claims C132-C136 provide interpretation of the structural features and their functional implications. Claim C134 is supported by 3DVA analysis (Video 6). The classification results are clear, and the interpretation of the helix-locked state as stabilizing the PA/MA relationship is logical based on the structural data.

results.result: The N-terminal region of NDUFS4 that forms the lock helix is not conserved in Y. lipolytica or mammals, suggesting it evolved after the split of Protostomia and Deuterostomia.
results.evaluation: Claims C137-C138 are supported by sequence comparison data (Figure 4—figure supplement 2). The evolutionary inference (C138) is logical based on the absence of this feature in both fungi (Y. lipolytica) and deuterostomes (mammals), suggesting it is specific to protostomes or a subset thereof. The sequence data clearly shows the lack of conservation.

results.result: Using the distance between NDUFAB1-α and NDUFA10 centers of mass as a metric, the helix-locked state resembles closed/active states while flexible class 1 resembles open/deactive states, with the first indication of direct PA-MA bridging via NDUFA10 and NDUFAB1-α in metazoans.
results.evaluation: Claims C142-C143 are supported by structural comparison using a specific distance metric (Figure 4—figure supplement 5). Claim C144 is supported by structural data showing potential salt-bridge formation. Claims C145-C146 provide context from previous studies and claim novelty for metazoans. The distance metric provides a quantitative basis for comparison, and the identification of direct bridging is supported by the structural data, though the weak density for NDUFAB1-α (noted in C144) introduces some uncertainty.

results.result: NDUFA5 and NDUFA10 remain in contact in both states but show state-dependent changes in their interaction, with R92A5 forming salt bridges with NDUFS4 (D34S4) in the helix-locked state and with NDUFA10 (E302A10) in the flexible state.
results.evaluation: Claims C147-C151 are supported by structural data (Figure 4, Video 6) showing specific interactions in each state. The identification of state-dependent salt-bridge partners for R92A5 is based on structural modeling of interactions. The structural data clearly shows the different arrangements, and the specific residue interactions are consistent with the observed conformations.

results.result: Conformational changes in loops adjacent to the CoQ reduction site differ between helix-locked and flexible states, with the TMH1-2ND3 loop well-ordered in helix-locked and partially disordered in flexible class 1, and TMH3ND6 α-helical in helix-locked but containing a π-bulge in flexible class 1.
results.evaluation: Claims C152, C155-C158 are supported by structural comparison data (Figure 5, supplementary figures) showing specific conformational differences in active site loops. The observations about TMH1-2ND3 loop ordering and TMH3ND6 secondary structure are based on clear structural data. Claim C158 provides mechanistic interpretation of the causes of these changes. The structural observations are well-documented.

results.result: In the helix-locked state, the C-terminal loop of NDUFA9 acts as a 'latch' binding atop the TMH1-2ND3 loop, trapping R50ND3 and forming multiple hydrogen bonds with ND1; in flexible class 1, this latch moves away, the loop becomes disordered, and most interactions are lost.
results.evaluation: Claims C159-C167 are supported by structural data (Figure 5C-F) showing specific interactions in each state. The 'latch' metaphor (C160) is an interpretive description of the structural arrangement. The structural data clearly shows the different arrangements of NDUFA9 and TMH1-2ND3 loop, the loss of density for R50ND3 in flexible state (C162), and the specific hydrogen bonding patterns (C164-C166). The inference about flexibility (C167) is logical.

results.result: The TMH3-4ND6 loop moves from 'untucked' in helix-locked to 'tucked' under NDUFA9 in flexible class 1, requiring ~10 Å translation of TMH4ND6, with similar latching and tucking behavior observed in C. thermophilum suggesting a general regulatory mechanism.
results.evaluation: Claims C168-C169 are supported by structural comparison data (Figure 5G-J, supplementary figures, Video 7) showing the movement of the loop and TMH4ND6. Claim C170 is supported by citation to a recent study in C. thermophilum. Claim C171 is speculation about generality based on observation in another species. The structural observations in Dm-CI are clear, and the comparison to C. thermophilum provides some support for generality, though this remains speculative without broader taxonomic sampling.
